facts.fact: Robert Trent Jones Jr., 2007, in a former sand and gravel mine on Puget Sound; host of the 2015 U.S. Open.
The Lone Fir behind the 15th green is the course's only tree.
The course's own emblem is two sails (avoided).

current.subject: The concrete gravel-plant ruins on a fescue dune (from the developer's photos).
current.keep: The ruins: the site's industrial past and an unusual shape.
current.weaknesses: Grey on grey; it floats without a setting at 1x.

concepts.name: The Ruins at Sundown
concepts.rationale: The ruins in silhouette against a Puget Sound sunset, on golden fescue: the same structure, now with light and a place.
concepts.symbolism: Industry turned to links; the evening light Chambers Bay is known for.
concepts.interpretation: The sunset colouring is atmosphere, not a specific view.
concepts.typography: Barlow Condensed SemiBold: industrial and clean.
concepts.strengths: Dramatic colour; owns its subject completely.
concepts.tradeoffs: A sunset roundel is a familiar resort format.

concepts.name: The Lone Fir
concepts.rationale: One Douglas fir on a fescue knoll, the Sound behind. The only tree on the course is its most photographed feature.
references: The Lone Fir behind the 15th green (fact)
concepts.strengths: Iconic, calm and true; reads at once.
concepts.tradeoffs: A single tree is a common golf emblem shape (avoid any look of Cypress Point).

recommendation: Concept 2. The Lone Fir is the course's own symbol in waiting; the ruins at sundown is the bolder colour if the industrial story should lead.
